feedback.answered: An attempt to observe the crash findings inside the replica's own event loop (rather than by calling the handler) did not reach the panic, and the reason is itself a behavioural detail worth recording. The loop spends about ten seconds in peer-latency measurement before it serves anything: ComputeClosestPeers performs twenty rounds of pings and sleeps half a second per round, so a started replica does not enter its select loop, and therefore does not accept client connections, for roughly that long. The harness waited only a couple of seconds and its queued commit was still unprocessed, which is why the run reported that the loop survived; the construction also showed that a listen failure is silent under a non-verbose logger, since the logger's Fatal prints and exits only when verbose. The process-death step of the crash findings therefore remains an inference from the run loop having no recover, while the ten-second measurement phase is now an observed startup property rather than an assumption.
remaining: observing the crash inside the loop would need a harness that waits out the measurement phase and provides a listener the sandbox permits, or a package-level injection point the implementation does not have
